newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end unchanged ahead of rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end unchanged ahead of rate decision.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed unchanged on Monday as the market awaited the Bank of Israel's decision on June interest rates after the close of the trading day, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.01 pct to 106.52
* CPI-linked government bonds: unchanged at 106.51
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.08 pct to 107.14
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.04 pct to 105.23
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 105.67
Volume including Makams was a very low 88 million shekels.
The Bank of Israel announced after trading ended for the day that it was holding its key lending rate for June at an annualised 13.9 percent.

"Demand for unlinked bonds continued to be strong on expectations of lower inflation over the summer months and lower interest rates," said Ilan Doron of Solid Financial Markets. "There was a lot of demand -- 175 million shekels against 2.5 million shekels supply."
"The behavior of the unlinked bonds indicated that the market expected a small cut in interest rates," said Ilan Shabat, a trader at Israel Discount Bank.
Analysts said the central bank's decision on the lending rate would cause prices to fall on Tuesday.

"Both the stock market and the bond market will be slightly disappointed by the (interest rate) decision, but not too much," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House, speaking after the announcement.
"I expect...prices of unlinked bonds and Makams to be lower tomorrow," he said.
Trading in CPI-linked bonds was mixed with a positive trend, but prices of most bonds ended unchanged, he said.

"The market has found a balance at yield levels of 4.2 percent. This kind of bond is less attractive than the unlinked bond because of expectations of low inflation for the summer months," Doron said. "The only thing that attracts investors to these bonds is the tight supply."
The government has been under less pressure to issue bonds because of slimmer budget deficit and a surge in privatisation revenue.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.40 shekels)
